utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-95-14/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen for the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You haven't got your microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen appearing for the Prosecutor with my colleague, Michelle Jarvis, and our case manager, Nikki Bonfield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For General Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mitko Naumovski, lawyer from Zagreb for Mr. Dario Kordic, and with me I also have my colleagues at Hunton Williams, Stephen Sayers, they were in telephone communication with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I hope that they can hear us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: We can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And for Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Bozidar Kovacic, lawyer from Croatia as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can each of the accused hear the proceedings in a language which they understand? General Kordic. THE APPELLANT KORDIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Thank you, yes, I can follow it all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Cerkez. THE APPELLANT CERKEZ: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can understand everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is a Status Conference being called in accordance with the provisions of Rule 65 bis. And so far as I can see, only for the purpose -- are there any matters which the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We don't have any particular matters we wish to raise. Everything has been fully briefed as far as we're concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do not have any particular questions we'd like to raise today. I merely wish to remind you of the salient matters that still await resolution. We do not have any new issues that we want to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you mean the application which you have made to see the documents which Mr. Cerkez has filed, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is one of the things, yes, correct. Mr. Sayers has prepared a list of these issues, and with your leave, he may remind us of what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are four matters that come to mind. This is an application to file a supplemental appellant's brief covering the Rule 68 violations that the Kordic Defence have made and that have been made by the Prosecution. As you pointed out, we're seeking access to the ex parte submissions made by Mr. Cerkez and by the Prosecution relating to the Rule 115 motions filed by Mr. Cerkez. In another case, our motions for access to a fourth set of Rule 115 submissions made by General Blaskic. Then there's the issue relating to

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As to the one in relation to the Blaskic proceedings, I'm afraid I have nothing to do with that here. That is a matter for the Appeals Chamber which is hearing the Blaskic case. The ex parte documents, we're still waiting for a response to the last of the matters so that they can both be heard together, or dealt with together. As to the filing supplementary brief in relation to the Rule 68 material, I had been anticipating an application for them to be tendered under Rule 115, but if that's not going to be done, then clearly you would be entitled to deal with it in a supplementary brief. But so far as I know, there is no such application presently filed. It may be on its way to us, but it hasn't arrived on my desk yet. But thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, there, Your Honour, we've received the closed session materials from the Blaskic case, the closed session testimony of General Blaskic, from the Prosecution. I got that about two days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It numbers hundreds of pages and we haven't had the opportunity yet fully to scrutinise it, but once we have, if that's going to be the subject of a Rule 115 motion, that motion will be expeditiously made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, you're breaking up a little bit. I'm not sure how good the telephone line is. How long ago did you get the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh. I see, all right. That's why we haven't got an application yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's right. And with respect to the AT material, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: We obviously do not have the AT materials, the additional material yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have you had a copy of the application for protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, I got that about an hour ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, so did I. Very well. Then we're fairly up to date by the look of it. But the one matter in relation to the ex parte documents, of course, which we have to consider with some care, is your standing to be heard on them. But that's a matter which, no doubt, will be dealt with when we give the decision. Any other matters? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, the Prosecution intends to file a response to the Kordic and Cerkez application for access to the ex parte documents filed by Cerkez, and we will be doing that on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I wasn't suggesting that you're out of time --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But we want to get the whole of that dealt with together.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one other matter I would like to raise, but unfortunately I would have to ask to go into closed session for that briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say closed session, you mean just with no sound? We've got a lot of people in the public gallery, which we can pull the blinds down if you want. Do you think they can lip read?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOELAERT-SUOMINEN
utterances.text: I don't think so. I'll turn my head towards you, so no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll treat it as the sound turned off for the public gallery until you've finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right, we are now back in public session. Is there anything else that anybody wants to raise? Well, thank you very much for coming. I hope you have a pleasant holiday weekend. It's a shame we had to be here for this afternoon. I'll adjourn now.
